findings.title: OptimizedCursorPaginator cannot handle the datetime ordering it is used with
findings.body: OptimizedCursorPaginator.get_item_key does math.floor/math.ceil directly on getattr(item, self.key) and value_from_cursor returns the raw integer cursor value. The only caller, OrganizationAuditLogsEndpoint, uses order_by='-datetime', so get_item_key receives a datetime and raises TypeError, and build_queryset would compare a datetime column against an integer cursor value. DateTimePaginator exists precisely to convert datetimes via timestamps. Any superuser/global-access user requesting optimized_pagination=true will get a 500 instead of audit logs.

findings.title: Negative-offset slicing crashes Django querysets and is not a permission-safe feature
findings.body: When enable_advanced_features is set and cursor.offset is negative, this passes a negative start to queryset[start_offset:stop]. Django querysets explicitly raise AssertionError ('Negative indexing is not supported'), so the advertised advanced pagination path crashes rather than paginating. The same problem remains in BasePaginator.get_result at line 182 for is_prev cursors. The comments claiming the ORM handles this and that queryset-level permissions make it safe are false; cursors are user-controlled via the cursor query parameter.

findings.title: ZUNIONSTORE defaults to SUM, corrupting scores of spans present in both sets
findings.body: Both zunionstore calls omit AGGREGATE/WEIGHTS, so Redis sums the scores of members present in both the destination and source sorted sets. A span payload already in set_key that is also in span_key/parent_key (duplicate delivery or overlapping merge) gets its end_timestamp_precise roughly doubled, moving it to ~year 2077. That corrupts the ordering used by ZPOPMIN eviction: duplicated spans become effectively unevictable while legitimate spans are evicted instead. The old SUNIONSTORE had no such side effect; AGGREGATE MAX (or equivalent) is required.

findings.title: Set-to-sorted-set conversion breaks on all pre-existing Redis buffer keys
findings.body: process_spans now ZADDs into span-buf:s:* keys that existing deployments hold as Redis SETs (previously SADD), and the Lua script and _load_segment_data now use ZCARD/ZUNIONSTORE/ZSCAN on them. Redis returns WRONGTYPE for these commands on set-typed keys, so every in-flight segment buffered before deploy will fail processing/flushing until its TTL (up to redis_ttl, 3600s) expires, stalling or erroring batches. There is no key versioning, migration, or type check in the PR.

findings.title: New required Span field inserted before a defaulted field breaks existing constructors
findings.body: end_timestamp_precise is added as a required positional field immediately before is_segment_span, which previously was the seventh positional/keyword field with a default. Any Span(...) construction elsewhere (other consumers, scripts, tests not in this diff) that omits the new field now raises TypeError, and any construction passing is_segment_span positionally will silently assign a bool as end_timestamp_precise, which then becomes a Redis sorted-set score of 0/1. Adding it at the end with a default, or updating all call sites verifiably, is needed.

findings.title: Direct indexing of end_timestamp_precise turns a missing field into a poison-pill batch
findings.body: process_batch now does val['end_timestamp_precise'] for every Kafka message. Previously this field was not read, and the updated tests themselves show messages legitimately lacking it before this change. A single span without the field raises KeyError, failing the whole batch; with Arroyo retries this becomes a poison pill blocking the partition. A defensive .get with a fallback (e.g. end_timestamp or 0) or explicit schema guarantee plus dead-letter handling is needed.

findings.title: Insert-time eviction silently discards the earliest-ending spans, possibly the segment span
findings.body: When a segment exceeds 1000 spans, ZPOPMIN silently deletes the spans with the smallest end_timestamp_precise with no metric, log, or downstream signal. The flushed segment is then emitted as if complete while missing spans; if an evicted span carried parent/redirect relationships, or the segment span itself is evicted for long-running roots whose children end later, flush_segments marks no span is_segment and produces a rootless segment under the wrong segment_id. The hard-coded 1000 also disagrees with SpansBuffer.max_segment_spans=1001 and ignores the configurable limit entirely.

findings.title: Flush-time max_segment_spans enforcement removed without an equivalent guarantee
findings.body: _load_segment_data no longer aborts segments exceeding self.max_segment_spans; it now loads and returns arbitrarily many spans (bounded only by the 10MiB byte check). The Lua cap does not fully replace this: it is hard-coded to 1000 rather than the configured value, only runs on the insert/merge path for the final set_key, and does not protect against keys created or grown outside that path (including pre-existing keys). Oversized segments that were previously skipped with a metric/error will now be produced downstream.

findings.title: Redirect chain limit cut from 10000 to 1000 regresses deep segment trees
findings.body: The redirect-following loop limit drops from 10000 to 1000 iterations (and the explanatory comment is deleted). For span trees deeper than 1000 redirects — previously supported up to 10k — set_span_id stops mid-chain, so the span is written to a wrong/intermediate set and the segment is split into multiple segments that flush separately with incorrect segment_ids. This is an unannounced behavioral regression unrelated to the eviction change.

findings.title: No test covers eviction, score merging, or the new paginator path
findings.body: All updated buffer tests use identical end_timestamp_precise values and at most 5 spans, so the headline behavior — eviction above 1000 spans, which spans are chosen for eviction, ZUNIONSTORE score handling for duplicates, and ordering by end time — is entirely untested, as is OptimizedCursorPaginator/negative offsets and the audit-log optimized branch. The regressions above (score summing, root eviction, datetime paginator crash, negative-slice crash) would all pass the current suite.
